p.src: Take a box of volume $V$. If the contents exert pressure $P$, then when the box expands by $dV$ the work done on the walls is $dE=-P\,dV.$ Now write the energy as $E=\rho V.$ Its differential is $dE=\rho\,dV+V\,d\rho .$ Equating the two expressions gives $\rho\,dV+V\,d\rho=-P\,dV,$ or $V\,d\rho=-(\rho+P)\,dV.$ Using $P=w\rho$, $V\,d\rho=-(1+w)\rho\,dV.$ Divide by $\rho V$: $\frac{d\rho}{\rho}=-(1+w)\frac{dV}{V}.$ Integrating, $\rho \propto V^{-(1+w)}.$ For a comoving cosmological box, $V\propto a^3,$ and therefore $\rho \propto a^{-3(1+w)}.$

p.src: How is this history inferred? We cannot see the future, but we can see the past. Looking to greater distance means looking to earlier time. zh: 最后，几何可以从最后散射面来检验。假设到该表面的距离已知。再假设能够在那里辨认出一个其物理大小已知得足够好的团块。那么就可以将该大小和距离与观测到的角大小进行比较。

p.src: In flat space the angle is the Euclidean one. In positively curved space it would appear larger; in negatively curved space, smaller. The analogy is ordinary surveying: take an object of known size at known distance and compare the measured angle with Euclidean geometry.
